issues.detail: Covers limits such as no resume option, false positives and WAF misses, but gives no guidance on handling errors like connection failures, timeouts, redirects to login pages, or rate-limit blocks.
The three examples are prompt-only descriptions with no commands or sample outputs, so they do not show concrete runnable usage.

scenarios.name: single-plugin-version-probe
scenarios.rationale: Both correctly recommend -p/--plugins WordPress with -a 3 and explain the reduced-request rationale well; B explicitly notes level 3 still requires permission (a rubric point A omits), giving it a slight edge.

scenarios.name: subdomain-pipeline-wordpress-extract
scenarios.rationale: B delivers a correct, complete pipeline matching every rubric requirement with accurate jq filtering and sensible caveats, while A refuses entirely and provides no commands.

scenarios.name: polite-bulk-scan-cidr
scenarios.rationale: Response A uses the CIDR target with --url-prefix https://, --no-errors, --wait, --max-threads, --log-brief and states that WhatWeb has no resume option with a split-and-rerun workaround, which covers nearly the whole rubric; Response B omits the CIDR target and --url-prefix, de-emphasizes --wait and recommends a log-subtraction resume instead of simply splitting the list, so it covers less of the rubric even though it also notes there is no resume and mentions chunking.
